articles.title: Wind warning for Calgary as gusts reach 100 km/h; warm, dry week ahead
articles.dek: Environment Canada issued a new yellow wind warning for Calgary on Sunday afternoon, with damaging gusts expected to ease in the evening ahead of a week of highs well above normal.
body: Environment and Climate Change Canada issued a yellow wind warning for the City of Calgary at 3:40 p.m. on Sunday, Nov. 8, rated as having a moderate impact [1]. The warning said damaging winds with gusts of 90 to 100 km/h would begin to ease in the evening [1].

At 5 p.m. Sunday, the weather station at Calgary International Airport recorded 11.1 C under mainly sunny skies, with a west wind of 43 km/h gusting to 66 km/h and relative humidity of 25 per cent [1]. The overnight forecast called for southwest winds of 40 km/h gusting to 60 km/h, and to 80 km/h at times in the early evening, before winds turn west and drop to 20 km/h gusting to 40 km/h overnight [1]. The low was forecast at 3 C [1].
Environment Canada advised residents to secure loose objects and asked people to report weather damage using the hashtag #ABStorm or by calling 1-800-239-0484 [1].

The rest of the week is forecast to stay dry and unusually mild [1]. Monday is expected to be mainly sunny with a high of 10 C, followed by a sunny 12 C on Tuesday [1]. Highs are forecast to climb to 17 C on Wednesday, Nov. 11, and 19 C on Thursday, before easing to 12 C on Friday and Saturday [1]. Overnight lows through the week are forecast to stay at or above freezing, between 1 C and 6 C [1].

Those temperatures are far above the seasonal normals Environment Canada lists for Calgary at this time of year, a high of 4 C and a low of -8 C [1]. The mild spell arrives while the city remains under Stage 4 outdoor water restrictions, which ban all outdoor watering of lawns, gardens, trees and shrubs, with an exception for edible crops, while the Bearspaw South Feeder Main is connected [2]. The City says Stage 4 began Nov. 4 and the shutdown is expected to last about four weeks [2].
Forecasts can change, and Environment Canada updates its warnings and forecast through the day [1].
key_facts: Yellow wind warning issued 3:40 p.m. Sunday; gusts of 90 to 100 km/h easing in the evening
Overnight low forecast at 3 C as winds turn west and ease
Highs forecast to reach 17 C Wednesday and 19 C Thursday; seasonal normal high is 4 C
Stage 4 outdoor water restrictions remain in effect

articles.title: City reports five fireworks incidents and three fines on first night of Diwali weekend
articles.dek: City, police and fire officials thanked residents for following Calgary's ban on personal fireworks as Diwali and Bandi Chhor Divas celebrations got underway.
body: The City of Calgary and its safety partners thanked residents, faith groups and cultural organizations on Sunday morning for helping keep Diwali and Bandi Chhor Divas celebrations safe, as festivities began across the city over the weekend [1].

According to the City, five fireworks incidents were reported on Saturday, Nov. 7, and three fines were issued [1]. The City did not say how much the fines were or where in the city the incidents took place [1].

Personal fireworks remain prohibited in Calgary [1]. The City said the ban applies to fireworks bought outside the city and to fireworks ordered online [1]. It encouraged community groups that want fireworks to use permitted, professionally operated displays, and pointed to a permitted professional show held on Nov. 5 at the Diwali in Huxley event [1].

The statement was issued on behalf of Calgary Fire Department Fire Marshal Glenn Baxter, Calgary Police Service Staff Sgt. Geoff Gawlinski and Damian Cole, the City's deputy chief of community safety [1]. Gawlinski said police had worked closely with community organizations and members ahead of the festival, adding, "we're grateful for their collaboration and partnership" [1]. The partners said they hope the level of compliance continues through the rest of the celebrations [1].

The City asks residents to call 911 for a fire or other emergency, and to call the police non-emergency line at 403-266-1234 to report fireworks that are happening now [1]. Fireworks that have already taken place can be reported through a 311 request under Disturbance and Public Behaviour Concerns [1].

Diwali and Bandi Chhor Divas fall on Sunday, Nov. 8, but some groups marked the occasion a day early [2]. On Saturday, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith and other government officials attended a celebration held at the Rio Banquet Hall in northeast Calgary [2].
key_facts: 5 fireworks incidents reported and 3 fines issued on Saturday, Nov. 7
Personal fireworks are banned in Calgary, including those bought elsewhere or online
Permitted professional show held Nov. 5 at Diwali in Huxley
Report current fireworks to police at 403-266-1234

articles.title: Cavalry FC rallies past FC Supra du Québec to reach CPL final, will host Atlético Ottawa on Nov. 21
articles.dek: A 2-0 win at Spruce Meadows overturned a first-leg loss and sends Calgary's Canadian Premier League club to the final at home.
body: Cavalry FC beat FC Supra du Québec 2-0 on Saturday, Nov. 7, in the second leg of their Canadian Premier League semifinal, earning a place in the league final [1][2]. Caniggia Elva and Ali Musse scored for Calgary [1].

Cavalry went into the match at ATCO Field at Spruce Meadows trailing after losing the first leg 2-1 in Québec [3]. Elva scored with a half-volley in the 25th minute, and Musse added a second goal around the hour mark, giving Cavalry a 3-2 win on aggregate [2]. Supra goalkeeper Joakim Milli saved a penalty from Musse during the match, having also stopped a penalty in the first leg [2]. Canadian Soccer Daily reported that a Cavalry player was sent off after a melee involving a ballboy [2].

Before the match, Culture Alberta reported that under the league's rules a Cavalry win by two or more goals would see the club host the final in Calgary [3]. Atlético Ottawa won the other semifinal, beating Forge FC 3-2 at home after extra time for a 5-4 aggregate win, with Nicolas Fleuriau Chateau scoring three goals [2].

The CPL final is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 21, at 1 p.m. Calgary time at ATCO Field, according to Canadian Soccer Daily, which described the match as a rematch between the two clubs [2]. The outlet noted the weather as a possible factor for a late-November match outdoors [2].
The same weekend, the Calgary Flames were scheduled to play at the Saddledome against the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday evening, after hosting the Anaheim Ducks on Friday [3].
key_facts: Cavalry 2, FC Supra du Québec 0 (3-2 on aggregate)
Goals by Caniggia Elva and Ali Musse
Final vs. Atlético Ottawa: Sat., Nov. 21, 1 p.m., ATCO Field

articles.title: Physicians now triaging patients at six Alberta emergency rooms after months of delay, premier says
articles.dek: Premier Danielle Smith said the emergency-room triage teams announced in January were in place as of Saturday.
body: Physicians are now triaging patients at six emergency departments across Alberta, Premier Danielle Smith said on Saturday, Nov. 7, during her province-wide radio show [1][2]. Smith said the triage teams were in place as of Saturday [1].

The provincial government announced the plan in January [1]. It followed the death of a 44-year-old man who waited nearly eight hours at the Grey Nuns Community Hospital emergency room in Edmonton to have his chest pain assessed; he died on Dec. 22, 2025 [1]. The Alberta Medical Association has said he was one of several patients who died around that time while waiting for care [1].

The rollout was delayed while the province and the Alberta Medical Association worked out operational details and physicians' contracts, The Canadian Press reported [1]. "It took longer than we hoped," Smith said [1].
The reports read for this article do not say which six emergency departments have the new triage teams, or whether any of them are in Calgary [1][2]. Calgary Insight could not confirm that detail.
A public inquiry into the Edmonton man's death is scheduled to resume in December [1].

Plan was announced in January after a patient's death in an Edmonton ER
Delays came from operational details and physician contracts
